A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeoDiffusion study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Brooklyn and Queens synthesis experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, ablations, and qualitative attention and panorama results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds conditioning ablations and quantitative panorama boundary-consistency results.

M1.justification: The method equations and architecture descriptions remain essentially unchanged. However, Figure 2 reroutes the training-only segmentation input from the geospatial attention extractor in v1 directly to the copied encoder in v2. The unchanged prose does not establish whether this represents an architectural change or a schematic correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Brooklyn and Queens panorama synthesis, including aligned and unaligned satellite inputs and near/far panorama conditions. The new boundary-consistency evaluation measures the existing synthesis task without adding a dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain Pix2pix, PanoGAN, and Sat2Density. Table 5 adds simpler conditioning and attention comparison variants. Table 6 includes PanoGAN alongside Sat2Density for seam evaluation, whereas v1's qualitative seam comparison in Appendix D used only Sat2Density.

E3.justification: The reported per-condition dropout probability changes from 0.5 to 0.1, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. Section 5.4 adds an LRCE evaluation using Depth Anywhere-derived depth gradients on 100 randomly sampled test panoramas. Existing dataset splits and principal evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Table 5 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence with tests removing training segmentation, replacing the geospatial adapter, concatenating conditions and noise spatially, and omitting geospatial information from attention. Section 5.4 adds quantitative seam analysis alongside the retained single-example visualization in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging the new seam metric over 100 panoramas introduces an evaluation sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive results on alternative conditioning designs and boundary consistency. For example, Table 5 reports PSNR 12.54 and FID 96.87 without training segmentation; Table 6 reports LRCE 0.0897 for PanoGAN, 0.0653 for Sat2Density, and 0.0436 for GeoDiffusion. Tables 1-4 and the two original Table 5 rows retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equations 1-5, the geospatial feature definitions, calibration assumptions, and camera models are retained. The added LRCE evaluation introduces no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and main conclusion retain the same claims: introducing mixed-view synthesis, proposing GeoDiffusion with geospatial attention, and achieving accurate, flexible synthesis from sparse panoramas and satellite imagery. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as supporting training-time segmentation supervision and newly identifies diffusion randomness as a challenge for consistency between adjacent viewpoints. The existing transient-object limitation moves from Appendix H into the expanded conclusion. Appendix D retains the qualification that outputs are not absolutely seamless.

D1.justification: Appendix B changes the reported hardware from two A100 GPUs to four A100 80GB GPUs, retains batch size 16, and removes the two-day convergence estimate. The dropout value is revised, and the abstract adds a project-page link; the PDFs alone do not establish what resources that page provides.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against Gaussian-splatting work and Sat2Scene, references for seam/depth evaluation, and an Appendix D distinction from Cylin-Painting and PanoDiffusion outpainting methods. These are targeted additions; the principal related-work structure and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include localized experimental discussion, a new Section 5.4, renaming the conclusion to include future work, moving and expanding the limitations paragraph, and updating author/header and citation presentation.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column journal format, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Figures 1-2 are rearranged or redrawn, Table 5 is expanded, and Table 6 is added. Existing qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional controls in Table 5 and quantitative seam evaluation strengthen evidence beyond v1's existing ablations and single seam illustration. The adjacent-view consistency limitation also improves qualification of the results. These gains are limited by the unexplained dropout revision, ambiguous Figure 2 rerouting, and removal of training-time information.
